answer: Hardware-backed remote attestation resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to anchor one identity to a chip-unique endorsement root inside a secure enclave before any cross-network voyage. Because valid quotes bind to distinct physical silicon and copper circuitry rather than cloned containers, attackers must pay real hardware procurement or enclave rental costs per identity. However, this relies on vendor root keys, leaving systems exposed to key leaks or bulk cloud TEE rentals.
